prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a slanted floor plane of blue climbing mats receding into a dark background climbing wall (4–6 m away), with a foreground person in a white 'Fly Emirates / JAMES 10' jersey standing within arm's reach (0.5–1.2 m) in front of the camera wearer across all 5 frames. In frames 1–3, a person in a striped shirt at the bottom-left edge (0.5–1 m), a person walking in a brown hoodie and white pants (2–3 m away, about 1.5 m behind the jersey wearer), a person sitting on the mat edge to the lower right (2–2.5 m away), and three distant climbers near the wall on the left (3.5–5 m) are clearly separated by brightness gradients. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera wearer turns and moves right as the jersey wearer approaches to within 0.4 m in frame 4—partially occluding a person in a dark jacket (1–1.5 m) and the striped-shirt person (1.5–2 m)—before turning away in frame 5 where a foreground hand enters at the bottom right (<0.5 m). The smooth luminance gradients clarify exact depth ordering and metric separation between overlapping people in frames 4–5 and the downward slope of the high-angle viewpoint better than RGB alone. However, the map is unreliable where face blurring in the RGB causes soft, distorted head contours in frames 1–3, and where the angled climbing wall and dark floor edges merge into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete person contours against the unlabelled gym floor and climbing wall, tracking up to eight people ranging from the foreground jersey wearer (0.5–1.2 m in front, within arm's reach) and partially cropped bystanders at the lower-left and lower-right edges (0.5–1.5 m) to mid-ground walkers (2–3 m) and distant climbers on the far left (3.5–5 m). In frames 1–3, the jersey wearer faces and looks generally toward the camera wearer while the seated person (2–2.5 m, lower right) faces the camera wearer from below eye level and background figures face away toward the left wall; in frames 4–5, the jersey wearer turns to face away and left while a person in a dark jacket (1 m, centre) faces the camera wearer next to the striped-shirt person facing away on the right (1.5 m). As the camera wearer shifts across the 5 frames, the masks capture changing occlusions, such as the jersey wearer blocking the seated person in frame 2, overlapping the dark-jacketed person in frame 4, and the camera wearer's own reaching hand appearing at the bottom of frame 5. The sharp mask boundaries disentangle tightly overlapping torsos in frame 4 and reveal distant background silhouettes in frames 1–2 that blend into the dark, hold-covered wall in RGB. However, the map is unreliable where it mislabels the blue-pants climber's feet as a 'skateboard' in frame 1, fragments the dark-jacketed person in frame 4, misclassifies the camera wearer's hand at the bottom of frame 5, and drops all mats, walls, and yellow storage bins.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is mostly blank across the 5 frames, detecting only the full yellow body skeleton of the person sitting on the blue mat edge (2–2.5 m in front and below eye level) in frames 1 and 3, plus isolated magenta hand skeletons at the bottom edge of frames 1, 2, and 5. In frames 1 and 3, the seated person's keypoints show them facing forward toward the camera wearer with bent knees, elbows resting near the legs, and both hands clasped together within their own lap, about 1–1.5 m to the right of the standing jersey wearer. The magenta hand clusters locate the jersey wearer's hanging right hand in frame 1 (about 1 m away, just within arm's reach) and hanging left hand in frame 2 (about 1 m away) as they shift left relative to the frame, as well as the camera wearer's own extended right hand at the bottom-right of frame 5 (<0.4 m). This map makes the exact joint articulation of the seated person's folded limbs and the precise finger orientation of the low, edge-cropped hands easier to read than in RGB alone. However, it is severely unreliable for scene-wide spatial understanding because it completely misses the standing foreground jersey wearer's body, all background and mid-ground people across all frames, and the seated person in frame 2 due to steep top-down foreshortening, motion, and partial occlusion at the frame boundaries.
